====== Start a business in Washington (LLC filing path) ======

**Washington · How do I start a business?** · state model checked by Claude · quality 1.00

//Generated by [[https://github.com/alibama/lexflow|lexflow]] from the state statutes (open-us-law, government publisher text) and checked by Claude: every quoted phrase was matched word for word against the statute text, and the process passed the BPMN/DMN schemas, bpmnlint and a Petri-net soundness check. Information, not legal advice.//

**Governing law:** [[https://apps.leg.wa.gov/rcw/default.aspx?cite=25.15.071|RCW 25.15.071]] — RCW 25.15.071: Formation—Certificate of formation.

  <bpmn:collaboration id="collab_wa_business" name="Start a business in Washington (LLC filing path)">
    <bpmn:documentation textFormat="text/plain">Someone wants to start a business, here as a limited liability company</bpmn:documentation>
    <bpmn:extensionElements>
      <lex:model id="wa-business" jurisdiction="wa" jurisdictionName="Washington" reviewStatus="draft" method="gold-manual">
        <lex:gap>Only the LLC filing path is modelled step by step (certificate of formation under RCW 25.15.071, filed under Article 2 of chapter 23.95 RCW). The other filed structures follow the same Article 2 filing rules (RCW 23.95.200, 23.95.225): a corporation or nonprofit corporation delivers articles of incorporation (RCW 23B.02.010, RCW 24.03A.090), a limited partnership is formed when the secretary of state files its certificate (RCW 25.10.201(3)), and the secretary of state must register an LLP that submits a completed application with the fee (RCW 25.05.500(4)). Their content checks are not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>No filing fee amount appears in the RCW: the secretary of state sets entity filing fees by rule (RCW 23.95.260, chapter 34.05 RCW), capped at the January 1, 2016 amounts, and the department of revenue sets trade name fees by rule, which may not exceed the actual cost of administering chapter 19.80 RCW (RCW 19.80.045). The amounts are in the Washington Administrative Code, which is not in the corpus.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Washington issues no separate certificate of organization: the LLC is formed when the secretary of state files the certificate of formation (RCW 25.15.071(2)(a)), and the secretary of state then delivers a copy of the filed record with an acknowledgment (RCW 23.95.225(2)). The filed copy is modelled as that delivery; a certificate of existence is available on request (RCW 23.95.235).</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The refusal deadline (fifteen business days after receipt, RCW 23.95.225(3)) runs from the date of receipt that the secretary of state must document (RCW 23.95.225(2)); the text gives no consequence for missing it, so it is marked 'unstated'. The remedy for a refusal is a petition to the superior court, with the filing and the secretary of state's explanation of the refusal attached (RCW 23.95.225(4)); the court's decision is not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The filing checks in filing_complies cover the certificate's required contents (RCW 25.15.071(1)(a)-(c), (f)) and the general execution, signer and fee rules (RCW 23.95.200(1)(d)-(e), (2)). Optional contents ((1)(d) dissolution date, (1)(e) other matters), the English-language and delivery-medium rules (RCW 23.95.200(1)(b)-(c)), and the name requirements of Article 3 of chapter 23.95 RCW (RCW 23.95.305) are not checked separately.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>After filing, a company doing business under a trade name must register it with the department of revenue (RCW 19.80.010), and a company requiring licenses incorporated into the system must apply for a business license (RCW 19.02.070(1)). Nothing in these sections orders the two: the model puts trade name registration first only as a modelling convention. The two conditions are not mutually exclusive, and the model's exclusive gateways take both paths only because uses_trade_name is evaluated first, in document order; this model has no inclusive split. In practice the department takes trade name registrations through the same business license application, which these sections do not say. Whether an LLC doing business only under its filed name 'uses a trade name' is open on the literal text: RCW 19.80.005(5) lists the filed names of domestic corporations and limited partnerships as true and real names but has no entry for limited liability company names, while RCW 19.80.010(3) sets the registration contents for an LLC.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>The business license application under chapter 19.02 RCW applies to persons 'requiring licenses that have been incorporated into the system'; which licenses those are, and when a city or state agency license or endorsement is needed, is outside these sections. The model routes the application through the regulatory agency when any requested license needs that agency's prelicensing review (RCW 19.02.070(3)-(4)); otherwise the business licensing service issues the license directly. An application can mix both kinds; the business license is then endorsed for the approved licenses, and the department advises the applicant of the status of the others (RCW 19.02.070(5)). The agency must advise the department 'within a reasonable time', which sets no fixed period, so no timer is modelled. The applicant's route to contest conditions or a denial (RCW 19.02.070(5)) is not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Local business licenses and taxes (city business license endorsements, business and occupation taxes) are not modelled; the local layer attaches at the business license step.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Professionals are not required to use a professional entity in every case; RCW 18.100.050 only authorizes one. Members of a professional LLC lose the shield to the extent required professional liability insurance or bond would have covered a claim (RCW 25.15.046(3)); professional discipline still applies (RCW 18.100.050(5)(b), RCW 25.15.046(7)).</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Later amendments of the certificate of formation (RCW 25.15.076) and annual reports (RCW 23.95.255) are outside these sections and not modelled.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>Nonprofit corporation status is a state corporate form, not tax exemption; federal 501(c) status and charitable solicitation registration are outside these sections.</lex:gap>
        <lex:gap>A delayed effective date (RCW 23.95.210(2): unless the organic law prohibits it, no more than ninety days after the date of filing) is not modelled.</lex:gap>

    <bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent id="petition_court" name="Petition court, attaching filing and refusal explanation">

===== Steps and the words they come from =====

  - **Execute certificate of formation** — Person executing the certificate of formation (founder) · //obligation// (§ 071(1)) \\ “//one or more persons must execute a certificate of formation//”
  - **Deliver certificate to secretary of state** — Person executing the certificate of formation (founder) · //obligation// (§ 071(1)) \\ “//The certificate of formation must be delivered to the office of the secretary of state for filing in accordance with Article 2 of chapter 23.95 RCW//”
  - **Pay filing fee set by rule** — Person executing the certificate of formation (founder) · //obligation// (§ 200(2)) \\ “//When an entity filing is delivered to the secretary of state for filing, any fee required under this chapter and any fee, interest, or penalty required to be paid under this chapter or law other than this chapter must be paid in a manner permitted by the secretary of state or by that law.//”
  - **Document date the filing was received** — Secretary of state · //obligation// (§ 225(2)) \\ “//The secretary of state shall document the date of receipt of an entity filing.//”
  - **Check certificate meets filing requirements** — Secretary of state · //obligation// (§ 200(1)) \\ “//To be filed by the secretary of state pursuant to this chapter, an entity filing must be received by the secretary of state, comply with this chapter, and satisfy the following//”
  - **File the certificate of formation** — Secretary of state · //obligation// (§ 225(1)) \\ “//The secretary of state shall file an entity filing that satisfies this chapter. The duty of the secretary of state under this section is ministerial.//”
  - **Deliver filed copy with acknowledgment** — Secretary of state · //obligation// (§ 225(2)) \\ “//After processing and accepting an entity filing, the secretary of state shall deliver to the person that submitted the filing a copy of the filed record with an acknowledgment of the date and time of processing.//”
  - **Return filing or notify refusal; explain in record** — Secretary of state · within 15 business days · //obligation// (§ 225(3)) \\ “//Return the entity filing or notify the person that submitted the filing of the refusal; and (b) Provide a brief explanation in a record of the reason for the refusal.//”
  - **Petition court, attaching filing and refusal explanation** — Person executing the certificate of formation (founder) · //permission// (§ 225(4)) \\ “//the person that submitted the entity filing may petition the superior court to compel its filing. The entity filing and the explanation of the secretary of state of the refusal to file must be attached to the petition.//”
  - **Register trade name with department** — Limited liability company · //obligation// (§ 010) \\ “//Each person or persons who carries on, conducts, or transacts business in this state under any trade name must register that trade name with the department as provided in this section.//”
  - **Submit business license application to department** — Limited liability company · //obligation// (§ 070(1)) \\ “//Any person requiring licenses that have been incorporated into the system must submit a business license application to the department requesting the issuance of the licenses.//”
  - **Include license fees and handling fee** — Limited liability company · //obligation// (§ 070(2)) \\ “//The applicant must include with the application the sum of all fees and deposits required for the requested individual license endorsements as well as the handling fee established by the department under the authority of RCW 19.02.075 .//”
  - **Notify regulatory agency of license application** — Department of revenue (business licensing service) · //obligation// (§ 070(4)) \\ “//Upon receipt of the application and proper fee payment for any license for which issuance is subject to regulatory agency action under subsection (3) of this section, the department must immediately notify the regulatory agency with authority to approve issuance or renewal of the license requested by the applicant.//”
  - **Advise department: approve, deny, or pending** — Regulatory agency with authority over the license · //obligation// (§ 070(4)) \\ “//Each regulatory agency must advise the department within a reasonable time after receiving the notice//”
  - **Issue business license with approved endorsements** — Department of revenue (business licensing service) · //obligation// (§ 070(5)) \\ “//The department must issue a business license endorsed for all the approved licenses to the applicant and advise the applicant of the status of other requested licenses.//”

===== Does the certificate of formation satisfy the filing requirements? =====

Decision table (DMN), hit policy FIRST.

^ Company name stated (RCW 25.15.071(1)(a); name rules in Article 3 of chapter 23.95 RCW) ^ Registered agent's name and address stated (RCW 25.15.071(1)(b)) ^ Principal office address stated (RCW 25.15.071(1)%%(c)%%) ^ Name and address of each person executing it stated (RCW 25.15.071(1)(f)) ^ Executed by or on behalf of an authorized person (RCW 23.95.200(1)(d)) ^ Name and capacity of each individual who executed it stated (RCW 23.95.200(1)(e)) ^ Required fees paid (RCW 23.95.200(2)) ^ → Secretary of state files the certificate ^ → Secretary of state refuses to file ^ Source ^
| false | - | - | - | - | - | - | false | true | § 071(1)(a) |
| - | false | - | - | - | - | - | false | true | § 071(1)(b) |
| - | - | false | - | - | - | - | false | true | § 071(1)(c) |
| - | - | - | false | - | - | - | false | true | § 071(1)(f) |
| - | - | - | - | false | - | - | false | true | § 200(1)(d) |
| - | - | - | - | - | false | - | false | true | § 200(1)(e) |
| - | - | - | - | - | - | false | false | true | § 200(2) |
| true | true | true | true | true | true | true | true | false | § 225(1) |

===== How does the regulatory agency advise the department on the requested license? =====

Decision table (DMN), hit policy UNIQUE.

^ Agency has finished its prelicensing investigation, inspection, testing or other review (RCW 19.02.070(3)) ^ Applicant meets the agency's requirements for the license ^ → What the agency advises the department ^ Source ^
| false | - | pending | § 070(4)(c) |
| true | true | approved; the agency advises the applicant of any specific conditions | § 070(4)(a) |
| true | false | denied; the agency gives the applicant reasons for the denial | § 070(4)(b) |

===== Which business structure fits, and what must be filed with the state? =====

Decision table (DMN), hit policy FIRST.

^ Organized for a nonprofit or charitable purpose ^ Owners render a licensed professional service ^ Number of owners ^ Owners want protection from the business's debts ^ Plans to sell shares to outside investors ^ Some co-owners will be passive investors only ^ → Business structure ^ → What is filed, and where ^ → State filing fee ^ Source ^
| true | - | - | - | - | - | Nonprofit corporation (chapter 24.03A RCW); incorporators must be individuals at least eighteen years old | Articles of incorporation, delivered to the secretary of state for filing | Set by secretary of state rule under RCW 23.95.260; no amount is stated in the RCW | § 090 |
| false | true | - | true | - | - | Professional service corporation (Title 23B RCW and chapter 18.100 RCW) or professional limited liability company (RCW 25.15.046); all owners must be licensed or otherwise legally authorized to render the same professional services in Washington, and one or more of them must be the incorporators (RCW 18.100.050(1)); architects, engineers and listed health care professionals have special rules (RCW 18.100.050(2), (3), (5)) | Articles of incorporation (professional service corporation) or certificate of formation (professional LLC), delivered to the secretary of state for filing | Set by secretary of state rule under RCW 23.95.260; no amount is stated in the RCW | § 050(1) |
| false | - | - | true | true | - | Stock corporation (Title 23B RCW) | Articles of incorporation, delivered to the secretary of state for filing | Set by secretary of state rule under RCW 23.95.260; no amount is stated in the RCW | § 010 |
| false | - | %%>%%= 2 | true | - | true | Limited partnership (limited partners are not personally liable for its obligations, even if they take part in management, RCW 25.10.321; a general partner is shielded only if the certificate elects limited liability limited partnership status, RCW 25.10.201(1)(d)) | Certificate of limited partnership, delivered to the secretary of state for filing | Set by secretary of state rule under RCW 23.95.260; no amount is stated in the RCW | § 201(1) |
| false | - | - | true | - | - | Limited liability company | Certificate of formation, delivered to the secretary of state for filing | Set by secretary of state rule under RCW 23.95.260; no amount is stated in the RCW | § 071(1) |
| false | - | 1 | false | - | - | Sole proprietorship | No formation filing; a person who does business under a trade name (a name that is not, or does not include, the owner's true and real name, or that suggests other parties, such as 'company' or 'and sons') must register it with the department of revenue | None to form; trade name registration fee set by department of revenue rule, not more than the actual cost of administering chapter 19.80 RCW (RCW 19.80.045) | § 010 |
| false | - | %%>%%= 2 | false | - | - | General partnership | No formation filing: two or more co-owners carrying on a business for profit form a partnership. A partnership doing business under a trade name must register it with the department of revenue. Optionally, the partnership may become a limited liability partnership by approving the terms by the vote needed to amend the partnership agreement and delivering an application to the secretary of state for filing (RCW 25.05.500(1)-(2)) | None to form; trade name registration fee set by department of revenue rule, not more than the actual cost of administering chapter 19.80 RCW (RCW 19.80.045); optional LLP application fee set by the secretary of state under RCW 23.95.260 (RCW 25.05.500(3)) | § 055(1) |

===== What the text leaves open =====

  * Only the LLC filing path is modelled step by step (certificate of formation under RCW 25.15.071, filed under Article 2 of chapter 23.95 RCW). The other filed structures follow the same Article 2 filing rules (RCW 23.95.200, 23.95.225): a corporation or nonprofit corporation delivers articles of incorporation (RCW 23B.02.010, RCW 24.03A.090), a limited partnership is formed when the secretary of state files its certificate (RCW 25.10.201(3)), and the secretary of state must register an LLP that submits a completed application with the fee (RCW 25.05.500(4)). Their content checks are not modelled.
  * No filing fee amount appears in the RCW: the secretary of state sets entity filing fees by rule (RCW 23.95.260, chapter 34.05 RCW), capped at the January 1, 2016 amounts, and the department of revenue sets trade name fees by rule, which may not exceed the actual cost of administering chapter 19.80 RCW (RCW 19.80.045). The amounts are in the Washington Administrative Code, which is not in the corpus.
  * Washington issues no separate certificate of organization: the LLC is formed when the secretary of state files the certificate of formation (RCW 25.15.071(2)(a)), and the secretary of state then delivers a copy of the filed record with an acknowledgment (RCW 23.95.225(2)). The filed copy is modelled as that delivery; a certificate of existence is available on request (RCW 23.95.235).
  * The refusal deadline (fifteen business days after receipt, RCW 23.95.225(3)) runs from the date of receipt that the secretary of state must document (RCW 23.95.225(2)); the text gives no consequence for missing it, so it is marked 'unstated'. The remedy for a refusal is a petition to the superior court, with the filing and the secretary of state's explanation of the refusal attached (RCW 23.95.225(4)); the court's decision is not modelled.
  * The filing checks in filing_complies cover the certificate's required contents (RCW 25.15.071(1)(a)-%%(c)%%, (f)) and the general execution, signer and fee rules (RCW 23.95.200(1)(d)-(e), (2)). Optional contents ((1)(d) dissolution date, (1)(e) other matters), the English-language and delivery-medium rules (RCW 23.95.200(1)(b)-%%(c)%%), and the name requirements of Article 3 of chapter 23.95 RCW (RCW 23.95.305) are not checked separately.
  * After filing, a company doing business under a trade name must register it with the department of revenue (RCW 19.80.010), and a company requiring licenses incorporated into the system must apply for a business license (RCW 19.02.070(1)). Nothing in these sections orders the two: the model puts trade name registration first only as a modelling convention. The two conditions are not mutually exclusive, and the model's exclusive gateways take both paths only because uses_trade_name is evaluated first, in document order; this model has no inclusive split. In practice the department takes trade name registrations through the same business license application, which these sections do not say. Whether an LLC doing business only under its filed name 'uses a trade name' is open on the literal text: RCW 19.80.005(5) lists the filed names of domestic corporations and limited partnerships as true and real names but has no entry for limited liability company names, while RCW 19.80.010(3) sets the registration contents for an LLC.
  * The business license application under chapter 19.02 RCW applies to persons 'requiring licenses that have been incorporated into the system'; which licenses those are, and when a city or state agency license or endorsement is needed, is outside these sections. The model routes the application through the regulatory agency when any requested license needs that agency's prelicensing review (RCW 19.02.070(3)-(4)); otherwise the business licensing service issues the license directly. An application can mix both kinds; the business license is then endorsed for the approved licenses, and the department advises the applicant of the status of the others (RCW 19.02.070(5)). The agency must advise the department 'within a reasonable time', which sets no fixed period, so no timer is modelled. The applicant's route to contest conditions or a denial (RCW 19.02.070(5)) is not modelled.
  * Local business licenses and taxes (city business license endorsements, business and occupation taxes) are not modelled; the local layer attaches at the business license step.
  * Professionals are not required to use a professional entity in every case; RCW 18.100.050 only authorizes one. Members of a professional LLC lose the shield to the extent required professional liability insurance or bond would have covered a claim (RCW 25.15.046(3)); professional discipline still applies (RCW 18.100.050(5)(b), RCW 25.15.046(7)).
  * Later amendments of the certificate of formation (RCW 25.15.076) and annual reports (RCW 23.95.255) are outside these sections and not modelled.
  * Nonprofit corporation status is a state corporate form, not tax exemption; federal 501%%(c)%% status and charitable solicitation registration are outside these sections.
  * A delayed effective date (RCW 23.95.210(2): unless the organic law prohibits it, no more than ninety days after the date of filing) is not modelled.
